findings.comment: Buildings 7 and 8 are located adjacent to the overhead utility line that crosses the property. However, no clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to the building faces are shown on the site plan or building elevations. Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance cannot be verified without dimension annotations and surveyed conductor elevations.

Customer facilities (Buildings 7 and 8) are proposed adjacent to overhead utility line with unknown conductor type (distribution vs. transmission). No 15-foot radial clearance dimensions are shown. Conductor type and voltage classification not specified on plans to determine which clearance standards apply.

Building elevation sheets are not provided in the site plan submittal. Without elevation views, building projections (overhangs, eaves, balconies) cannot be verified for compliance with 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from the overhead conductor.

No building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations are provided. The overhead utility line visible on the existing conditions survey lacks surveyed elevation data on building elevations, preventing verification that required clearances are maintained.

No section or plan view exhibits with dimension annotations from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edges of buildings, parking areas, driveways, or retaining walls are provided. Clearance verification dimensions are entirely missing from all relevant plan sheets.

Retaining walls are proposed along the southern boundary in close proximity to the overhead utility line shown on the existing conditions survey. However, no clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to the wall face are provided. Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance cannot be verified.

Section views for retaining walls (Sheet 38) do not show the overhead utility line or clearance dimensions from the outer conductor to the wall face. Cross-section details for clearance verification from conductor to outermost edge of walls are missing.

applicableAreas: Driveways crossing or adjacent to overhead line
findings.comment: Driveways are shown on the proposed site plan in the area where the overhead utility line crosses the property. No vertical clearance dimensions from the lowest point of the overhead conductor (including any attachments) to the finished driveway grade are provided. Mid-span clearance verification is missing.

applicableAreas: Entire site plan area with overhead utility line
findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on any plan sheets (site plan, grading plan, wall plan, or sections) for the overhead utility line. Applicant has not provided ANY dimension annotations measuring clearances from the outside conductor to site features. Without dimensions, it is impossible to verify if measurements are from the conductor or from the pole centerline.

applicableAreas: Public sidewalk at southwest corner near overhead utility line
findings.comment: A public sidewalk is proposed along the western street frontage (Valley View Road) that intersects/crosses under the overhead utility line path near the southwest corner of the property. No vertical clearance dimensions are provided where the sidewalk passes under the overhead line. Whether power poles/fixtures adjacent to the sidewalk create obstructions or clearance concerns cannot be verified.

The overhead utility line crosses the site at elevations where proposed driveways and building areas are located, creating potential vertical clearance concerns. However, no registered surveyor data is provided showing pole locations and mid-span clearances. Survey of conductor elevation is necessary to verify minimum vertical clearances are maintained.

applicableAreas: Tree plantings along overhead utility line path at southern boundary
findings.comment: Proposed tree canopies are shown directly along and intersecting the path of the overhead utility line on the landscape plan. The landscape plan does not provide species verification confirming that proposed trees are utility-compatible (UC-marked in ECM Appendix F with mature height ≤20 feet) as required within 10 lateral feet of distribution conductors. No clearance dimensions are provided between tree locations and the overhead conductor. Plant species for mitigation trees must be verified for utility-compatibility.

No plan note requiring owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines is present on the cover sheet or general notes. This notification requirement is mandated by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 and must be included on all plans with overhead electric facilities.
